summary: Isle Royale's first lighthouse, built 1855 for the copper mines; put out 1859, relit 1874, closed for good 1879. The tower stands in Isle Royale National Park.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The station record gives 213.4 m, which is 700 feet, and the USLHS roster gives 700 feet. Terry Pepper gives a focal plane of 70 feet and LighthouseFriends 65 feet, so 700 feet is almost certainly a unit or entry error (see corrections).
The National Register nomination and the Park Service give 1928 to 1939; LighthouseFriends gives 1927 to 1939. The story uses 1928 from the two sources that agree.

corrections.why: The record's 213.4 m equals 700 feet. Terry Pepper gives the focal plane as 70 feet above lake level (21.3 m); LighthouseFriends gives 65 feet (19.8 m). The USLHS record carries the same 700-foot figure, so the error probably starts there.
The National Register nomination describes a slightly tapered cylindrical light tower of rubble stone and brick, 50 feet high, not a conical one.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-22: story corrected against the cached sources. Changed: construction dates (Terry Pepper's 'the following year' follows the 1854 navigation-season plan, so it is 1855, not 1854); the lead's 'dimmed' (the sources say shut down or extinguished in 1859); the 1872 Whiting request moved before the 1874 relight (it was December 1872, during the dark years); 'the station sat mostly dark after 1879', which no source says in those words (the NRHP says 'again abandoned until the turn of the century'); the 'park took over in 1939' wording (Terry Pepper and the Park Service date the national park, LighthouseFriends 1940); the dormer date (the nomination says 'may have been added circa 1910'); 'the engineer' is Orlando Poe (LighthouseFriends); the Kruger supply source is the Island Mining Company at Siskiwit; the Park Service gives 14 miles in its history section and 15 in its summary (both now stated); the access paragraph (LighthouseFriends: boat; Terry Pepper's page dated 12/02/2007: trail). Units added. Not checked against a Board report: the 1902 request and the 1879 inspection rest on LighthouseFriends alone (the local corpus starts in 1891, per the notes below). Thin on primary sources for 1852 to 1879: the local Lighthouse Board corpus begins in 1891, and the Chronicling America search for Rock Harbor light in Michigan papers 1855 to 1880 returned only two weather pages (not used). The story rests on the National Register nomination (digitized, prepared 1976), the Park Service article, Terry Pepper's history, LighthouseFriends (facts; its Kruger letter and 1872-1879 inspection passages are second-hand) and the USLHS roster. The USLHS 'Pages from the Past' Keepers Log PDF (1993) was not read. First lighting: Park Service says completed and lit 1855; Terry Pepper and LighthouseFriends place the Petty arrival and first exhibition in 1856. Relit date: 5 August (Terry Pepper), 25 July (LighthouseFriends), August (Park Service). Lens: the record dates a lens installation to 1875, but Terry Pepper's 1874 account has the station's Fourth Order lens in use when the light was relit; the record's date is not supported. Isle Royale NP established 1939 (Park Service, Terry Pepper) or 1940 (LighthouseFriends); the story says the Park Service date. The Park Service page on Rock Harbor says Isle Royale lighthouses are listed on the National Register; the listing year is not confirmed beyond the record's 1977 and the NPGallery reference number. Access: LighthouseFriends says by boat; Terry Pepper says a trail system makes it easy to reach. The story says to check current park information. No storm, wreck or rescue at this station is named in the sources read, so the story has no storms chapter.
